body_html:
Mother’s Day messages in Spanish are a lovely way to make the second Sunday in May extra special, whether you are writing to your own mom, a Spanish-speaking mother-in-law or a friend who just became a mom. In Spanish, the day is el Día de las Madres, and in Spanish-speaking families it is one of the most important celebrations of the year. If your partner’s family is Mexican, there is one thing to know: many Mexican and Mexican-American families also celebrate on May 10, whatever the day of the week. Below are thirty-five messages for your mom, grandmother, mother-in-law and the moms in your life, with English translations.

Quick answer
  • Basic: ¡Feliz Día de las Madres!
  • For your mom: Gracias por todo, mamá. Te quiero mucho.
  • For your mother-in-law (formal): Feliz día, suegra. Gracias por recibirme en su familia.
  • In the US, Mother’s Day is the second Sunday in May. Mexican families often celebrate on May 10 as well.
{{toc}}

Short Mother’s Day messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Feliz Día de las Madres!
    Happy Mother’s Day!
  2. ¡Feliz día, mamá!
    Happy day, Mom!
  3. Gracias por todo, mamá. Te quiero mucho.
    Thank you for everything, Mom. I love you very much.
  4. Eres la mejor mamá del mundo.
    You’re the best mom in the world.
  5. Todo lo que soy te lo debo a ti.
    Everything I am, I owe to you.
  6. Feliz día a la mujer más fuerte que conozco.
    Happy day to the strongest woman I know.

You will also see el Día de la Madre, singular. Both forms are correct; el Día de las Madres is the one most Mexican and Mexican-American families use, and el Día de la Madre is common in Spain.

Heartfelt messages for your mom

  1. Gracias por tus desvelos, tus consejos y tu amor sin condiciones.
    Thank you for your sleepless nights, your advice and your unconditional love.
  2. Aunque esté lejos, mi corazón está contigo hoy.
    Even though I’m far away, my heart is with you today.
  3. Cada día entiendo un poco más todo lo que hiciste por mí.
    Every day I understand a little more of everything you did for me.
  4. Gracias por enseñarme a ser fuerte y a nunca rendirme.
    Thank you for teaching me to be strong and never give up.
  5. Eres mi ejemplo, mi refugio y mi mejor amiga.
    You’re my role model, my safe place and my best friend.
  6. Si pudiera elegir, te elegiría como mamá otra vez.
    If I could choose, I would choose you as my mom again.
  7. Mamá, gracias por creer en mí cuando yo no lo hacía.
    Mom, thank you for believing in me when I didn’t.
{{image:2}}

For your grandmother, mother-in-law and other moms

  1. Feliz Día de las Madres, abuelita. Gracias por tanto amor.
    Happy Mother’s Day, Grandma. Thank you for so much love.
  2. Feliz día, suegra. Gracias por recibirme en su familia con tanto cariño.
    Happy Mother’s Day, mother-in-law. Thank you for welcoming me into your family so warmly. (formal)
  3. A la mamá de mis hijos: gracias por todo lo que haces cada día.
    To the mother of my children: thank you for everything you do every day.
  4. Feliz día a todas las mamás de la familia.
    Happy day to all the moms in the family.
  5. Feliz Día de las Madres, tía. Siempre has sido como una segunda mamá.
    Happy Mother’s Day, Auntie. You’ve always been like a second mom.
  6. Feliz primer Día de las Madres, amiga. ¡Vas a ser una mamá increíble!
    Happy first Mother’s Day, my friend. You’re going to be an amazing mom!

With a mother-in-law, usted is often the safe choice, at least at first; see {{link:talking-to-your-in-laws-in-spanish|talking to your in-laws in Spanish}}.

Funny Mother’s Day messages

  1. Gracias por no venderme cuando era adolescente.
    Thank you for not selling me when I was a teenager.
  2. Mamá, perdón por todas las veces que dije “ahorita voy”.
    Mom, sorry for all the times I said “I’m coming in a minute”.
  3. Ya entendí por qué decías “cuando seas mamá me vas a entender”.
    I finally understand why you said “you’ll understand when you’re a mom”.
  4. Feliz día a la única persona que encuentra todo lo que yo pierdo.
    Happy day to the only person who finds everything I lose.

The second one is a joke about ahorita; see {{link:mexican-slang|Mexican slang}} if it doesn’t make sense yet.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

For a mom who is no longer here

  1. Hoy y siempre te llevo en mi corazón, mamá.
    Today and always, I carry you in my heart, Mom.
  2. Te extraño cada día, pero hoy un poco más.
    I miss you every day, but today a little more.
  3. Gracias por todo lo que me enseñaste. Sigues conmigo.
    Thank you for everything you taught me. You’re still with me.

For words to support a friend on this day, see {{link:condolences-in-spanish|condolences in Spanish}}.

If your family is Mexican: May 10

In the United States, Mother’s Day falls on the second Sunday in May. In Mexico, it is always May 10, and many Mexican-American families keep that date too, sometimes celebrating twice. Many schools hold festivals where children perform for their mothers, restaurants are fully booked, and some families hire mariachis to sing Las Mañanitas early in the morning. Many workplaces give mothers the afternoon off. If you have a Mexican partner, ask early what the family is planning: ¿Qué van a hacer para el diez de mayo?

The Mexican government portal publishes official notes on the day each year, which is a good way to practice reading.

{{image:3}}

Tips and common mistakes

  • Feliz día de madre. Use the article: Feliz Día de las Madres or Feliz Día de la Madre.
  • Missing the second date. In the US, it is the second Sunday in May. If your partner’s family is Mexican, ask whether they also celebrate on May 10.
  • Using tú with a formal mother-in-law. Follow the family’s lead; usted is safer at first.
  • Forgetting the subjunctive in wishes. Que pases un día precioso, not que pasas.
{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

A Mother’s Day message in Spanish doesn’t need to be long to be meaningful. Choose a line that sounds like you, add a memory, and if your partner’s family is Mexican, ask about May 10 too. For more family moments, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say Happy Mother’s Day in Spanish?
faq.a: ¡Feliz Día de las Madres! You will also hear ¡Feliz Día de la Madre!

faq.q: Why do some families celebrate Mother’s Day on May 10?
faq.a: In Mexico, Mother’s Day is always May 10, and many Mexican-American families in the US keep that date, alongside or instead of the second Sunday in May.

faq.q: What do you write to your mother-in-law on Mother’s Day?
faq.a: Something warm and polite, often with usted: Feliz día, suegra. Gracias por recibirme en su familia.

faq.q: What is a short Mother’s Day message in Spanish?
faq.a: Gracias por todo, mamá. Te quiero mucho.
